license_note: The Tor Project builds its released binaries with --enable-gpl (configure.ac: 'allow the inclusion of GPL-licensed code, building a version of tor and libtor covered by the GPL rather than its usual 3-clause BSD license'), so the daemon Canalla ships is covered by the GPL. Tor's own code is BSD-3-Clause; the bundle's docs/tor.txt lists the components.
comment: The Tor Project's official *expert bundle*: the tor daemon only. No browser, no pluggable transports and no control port are shipped. Every archive is pinned by size and SHA256 here, and scripts/fetch-tor-runtime.py refuses to stage anything that does not match. The pins themselves come from the Tor Project's signed checksums file; scripts/verify-tor-runtime-pin.py re-checks that provenance (including the detached GPG signature) so a pin can never silently drift from the official release. The Tor Project *removes* superseded release directories (15.0.24 answered 404, and on 2026-11-09 the whole 15.0.25 directory was removed too: the pinned URL returned a 306-byte 404 page), so a stale pin reads as a hard FAIL here — that is the signal to re-pin, not to relax the check. 16.0 is the current supported release and the only version directory published at dist.torproject.org/torbrowser.
